html:
The Warraskoyack were an Algonquian tribe on the south bank of the James River in Virginia, in what is now Isle of Wight County. In the early 1600s they belonged to the Powhatan paramount chiefdom.

They farmed maize and fished, and lived across the river from the English fort at Jamestown after 1607. They traded food to the colonists in the early years, but after the Powhatan attack on the colony in 1622 the English burned their towns. English planters then took their land, and the county created there in 1634 was named after them. The tribe faded from the records soon after. Their neighbours included the Nansemond to the east and the other chiefdoms of the Virginia tidewater.
